r.x: Most festivals book the names you already know. We book the ones you’re about to.
r.alt: Geese on a small stage in 2024, the crowd close

r.x: Step into an architectural wonderland, built by hand into the forest. When it’s over, it all finds a new home.
r.alt: The Galaxy courtyard lit at night, full of people

r.x: This isn’t a festival your kids put up with. They get a camp of their own in the woods.
r.alt: Families singing together at the Coyote stage

r.x: Four days of music, and you’ll go home rested. Morning yoga under the firs, trails and quiet corners.
r.alt: Morning yoga outside at the Courtyard

r.x: Skip the food-truck line. Sit down at a long table with a chef and a band.
r.alt: Glasses raised at a long Curation brunch table

r.x: Local beer, a cocktail, a good coffee, and you never have to leave the music to get one.
r.alt: The Pickathon Bar, busy in the afternoon

r.x: No parking-lot campground. Your tent goes under giant firs, a short walk from the music.
r.alt: Campers in the shade between tents and tall firs

r.x: The headliner ends. The woods don’t. Dance under the trees long after.
After dark, the forest lights up with art you stumble onto around every bend.
r.alt: Glowing light pillars in the trees at night

r.x: Touring comics in a barn small enough to heckle back.
r.alt: A comic on stage in the Lucky Barn

r.x: Stories and poems read aloud under the trees. Bring nothing but time.
r.alt: Spoken word on the Woods stage

r.x: Take home something made by hand, by the person who made it.
r.alt: The Mercantile lit at dusk, people walking through

zero.x: Reusable dishes and steel cups all weekend. Single-use dishes have been gone since 2011.

eras.x: Four eras. Every year has its own poster.

r.x: A one-day benefit for KBOO, run by volunteers.
Pendarvis Farm becomes home, and students start building the stages.
No festival in 2020 or 2021, then back in 2022 as neighborhoods.
A 10-year permit, and Creative Neighborhoods starts building to last.
